device.manufacturer: Xiamen Print Future Technology Co., Ltd
device.name: Fichero / AiYin D11 Thermal Label Printer
device.notes:
Compact thermal label printer sold as Fichero D11s / AiYin D11. Price $15-20. 96px printhead at 203 DPI. Li-Ion battery with USB-C charging. Also supports Classic Bluetooth SPP, but BLE is the preferred transport.
PROTOCOL: exposes 4 BLE UART services that are functionally interchangeable for printing. The vendor app uses only service 0xFF00: it connects, picks the service whose UUID starts with 0000ff00, takes the writable characteristic (0xFF02) and two notify characteristics (0xFF01 responses, 0xFF03 credit/MTU flow control); no 0x18F0 reference exists anywhere in the app. The 0x18F0 service (write 0x2AF1, notify 0x2AF0) is the one third-party client 0xMH/fichero-printer treats as primary, and it also works. Info and config commands use the AiYin command format (10 FF prefix). Raster printing uses standard ESC/POS GS v 0 (1D 76 30) header with 1-bit BMP data, MSB first, 12 bytes/row.
DEVICE CLASS: this is AiYin class — enable/stop commands are 10 FF FE 01 / 10 FF FE 45. The SDK also supports Lujiang-class devices that use 10 FF F1 03 / 10 FF F1 45. Using the wrong class = silent failure (printer accepts data but never prints).
PRINT SEQUENCE: set_density → set_paper_type → wake_up (12 null bytes) → enable_printer → raster_header + pixel_data → form_feed → stop_print. Stop print waits for 0xAA or "OK" response (60s timeout).
STATUS BITMASK (response to 10 FF 40): Bit0=printing, Bit1=cover open, Bit2=no paper, Bit3=low battery, Bit4=overheated(alt), Bit5=charging, Bit6=overheated. 0x00 = ready.
COMMANDS (10 FF family; newly evidenced in the current vendor app, app-confirmed not hardware-tested): paper type 10 FF 84 nn (its set-label-paper call); density 10 FF 10 00 nn (set-density); battery query 10 FF 50 F1; model 10 FF 20 F0 / version 10 FF 20 F1 / serial number 10 FF 20 F2 (its model, version and serial-number queries).
SUPPORTED: Any of the 4 UART services works. The vendor app uses 0xFF00; 0x18F0 is the functional alternate used by third-party clients and is recommended for cross-model compatibility.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for all info/config commands (verified against D11s hardware with firmware 2.4.6), the print sequence, raster format, and status bitmask. Sourced from 0xMH/fichero-printer — itself reverse-engineered from an older build of the vendor app — and re-verified against the current app for the 0xFF00 service selection, 0xFF03 credit/MTU flow control, the added 10 FF opcodes, and the OTA flow (all app-confirmed, not hardware-tested).
ECOSYSTEM: the Fichero Printer app is a Karsten International white label of the LuckPrinter SDK app; sibling rebrands include Lidl's Pocket Printer and "Luck Jingle". The L13 sibling (sold by Lidl as Silvercrest, same OEM) was independently reverse-engineered by atctwo and confirms the command family on real hardware: YiChip YC3121-D MCU, FCC ID 2A6FW-L13, and a USB-C port that doubles as a USB printer device. An AiYin OTA firmware-update protocol (10 FF E0 AA AA to enter update mode, then 1B 10-framed 256-byte chunks) is documented in 0xMH's PROTOCOL.md; that writeup is an accurate transcription of the vendor app's update flow (app-confirmed in the current app's firmware-update and response-parsing paths), still not hardware-tested. No public firmware images exist.

factory_reset.effect: Send factory reset command 10 FF 04. Returns "OK". Power-cycling also resets the connection.

methods.description: Scan for "FICHERO" or "D11s_" BLE advertisement, connect, and follow the documented print sequence.

steps.action: Power the printer and scan for its advertisement.
Connect to service 0xFF00 (as the vendor app does) or 0x18F0 (as third-party clients do); any of the 4 UART services works.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Device advertises when powered on. No pairing or bonding required. The vendor app connects to the 0xFF00 BLE UART service (app-confirmed in v1.1.17); third-party clients such as 0xMH's use 0x18F0, which also works.

rejoin.notes: No persistent bonding. Any central can connect.

dfu_mode.notes: Not established: whether the printer re-advertises or keeps the connection in update mode is not recorded.

enter.notes: 10 FF E0 AA AA on the command characteristic.

image.notes: No public firmware images exist; where the vendor app gets them is not recorded here.

dfu.notes: The AiYin-class OTA protocol: after enter_update_mode, the image is sent in 1B 10-framed 256-byte chunks. Documented in 0xMH/fichero-printer's PROTOCOL.md and app-confirmed in the current app's firmware-update and response-parsing paths; not hardware-tested. The chunk header beyond 1B 10 and the response codes are not transcribed here.

helpful_urls.description: Manual for the D11 platform this printer is built on — the Fichero is an AiYin D11s underneath. Archived because the live host refuses automated requests.
helpful_urls.title: NIIMBOT D11 wireless label printer manual (Internet Archive)

remaining_unknowns: No command byte here has been run against hardware by this project: every `verification: reported` rests on 0xMH/fichero-printer (hardware-tested on a D11s, fw 2.4.6) and the vendor app's builders.
Whether the print_raster stream tolerates the credit-paced 20-byte writes of 0xFF02 without the 0xMH 20 ms gap is app-inferred, not measured.
10 FF C0 nn (set speed) answers four bytes nobody has decoded; it is left out of `commands` rather than declared with a guessed range.

enable_printer.description: 10 FF FE 01 — AiYin-class 'start print job' (step 4). The Lujiang-class equivalent is enable_printer_lujiang; sending the wrong class makes the printer accept the raster and never print.

enable_printer_lujiang.description: 10 FF F1 03 — the Lujiang/base-class 'start print job' (L13, LuckP/DP series siblings). NOT for the D11s, which needs enable_printer; kept so a Lujiang-class sibling is a spec edit, not a code change. Hardware-confirmed by atctwo on the L13.

enter_update_mode.advanced_reason: Switches the printer into firmware update mode. No public firmware image exists, so there is nothing to finish the update with; how the printer leaves the mode without one is not established.
enter_update_mode.description: 10 FF E0 AA AA — put the printer into its firmware update mode; the image then follows in 1B 10-framed 256-byte chunks (see features[firmware_update]). From 0xMH's PROTOCOL.md and the vendor app's update flow; not hardware-tested.

factory_reset.advanced_reason: Clears the stored density, paper-type and auto-shutdown settings. Nothing is lost that a client cannot re-send: run set_density, set_paper_type and set_shutdown_time again afterwards.
factory_reset.description: 10 FF 04 — restore factory settings; replies 'OK'. Also the command behind setup.factory_reset.

feed_dots.description: 1B 4A nn — feed forward by nn dots (ESC J).

dots.description: Dots to feed (203 dpi: 8 dots per mm).

form_feed.description: 1D 0C — advance to the next label / tear position (step 6). 0xMH waits ~300 ms after it before stop_print. 10 0C is an alternate form feed that replies 'OK'.

get_battery.description: 10 FF 50 F1 — two bytes [status, percent], e.g. 00 56 = 86 %.

get_status.description: 10 FF 40 — one status byte: bit0 printing, bit1 cover open, bit2 no paper, bit3 low battery, bit4 overheated (alt), bit5 charging, bit6 overheated; 0x00 = ready. Poll before a job.

print_raster.description: ESC/POS GS v 0 raster (step 5): 1D 76 30 m xL xH yL yH followed by width_bytes × height_rows bytes of 1-bit rows, MSB = leftmost pixel, 1 = black. Width is in BYTES (12 = the 96-dot head, fixed on the D11s), height in rows; both uint16 little-endian. The whole command is one byte stream the transport chunks — 200-byte writes 20 ms apart on 0x2AF1 (0xMH), 20-byte credit-paced packets on 0xFF02 (vendor app) — so `bitmap` may exceed one write. Wait ~500 ms after the last chunk before form_feed.

bitmap.description: width_bytes * height_rows bytes of 1-bit rows, MSB first, 1 = black.

height_rows.description: Row count; a 30 mm label at 203 dpi is 240 rows.

mode.description: GS v 0 scaling mode; the app sends 0.

width_bytes.description: Row width in bytes; 12 (96 dots) on the D11s — the set-width command is ignored by this model.

set_density.description: 10 FF 10 00 nn — print darkness (step 1). Replies 'OK'; 0xMH waits ~100 ms after it before the next command. The codes are declared on the image_upload feature's print_density.

set_paper_type.description: 10 FF 84 nn — tell the printer what stock is loaded (step 2), so form_feed advances to the right mark. Replies 'OK'. Codes declared on the image_upload feature's paper_type.

set_shutdown_time.description: 10 FF 12 HH LL — auto power-off delay in minutes, uint16 BIG-endian; replies 'OK'. 10 FF 13 reads it back.

minutes.description: Minutes of idle before power-off; the unit ships at 20.

stop_print.description: 10 FF FE 45 — AiYin-class 'end print job' (step 7). Wait for a reply of 0xAA or the ASCII 'OK' on the notify characteristic, with a 60 s timeout; the label is cut/positioned when it arrives.

stop_print_lujiang.description: 10 FF F1 45 — the Lujiang/base-class 'end print job'; pairs with enable_printer_lujiang. NOT for the D11s.

wake_up.description: Twelve 0x00 bytes — wakes the print engine before enable_printer (step 3 of the print sequence). The vendor app and 0xMH both send exactly twelve.

characteristics.name: Write
characteristics.notes: Write channel (the app picks the characteristic with the write property in this service). The vendor app writes in packets of 20 bytes by default (raised after MTU negotiation — max_chunk_size states the pre-negotiation floor), paced by credits received on 0xFF03. The four UART services are interchangeable, so the `commands` here are the SAME block the 0x2AF1 characteristic declares (a YAML anchor, not a copy): byte values from 0xMH/fichero-printer's docs/PROTOCOL.md and fichero/printer.py, hardware-tested by that project on a D11s (fw 2.4.6) and app-confirmed here — `reported`, not run by this project.

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: Notification channel for responses. Subscribe before sending commands. Responses are ASCII strings or binary status bytes.

characteristics.name: Notify (Credit/MTU)
characteristics.notes: Credit/MTU flow-control channel (app-confirmed in v1.1.17, not hardware-tested). The app treats it as its credit channel. A 2-byte message starting with 0x01 adds that many send credits; a 3-byte message starting with 0x02 carries the device's requested MTU, which the app negotiates upward. The write loop blocks until credit > 0 and spends one credit per packet. Also enumerated on the L13 sibling.

services.name: Fichero UART Service (Vendor Primary)
services.notes: Service used by the vendor app (it selects the service whose UUID starts with 0000ff00). All commands are written to 0xFF02; responses arrive as notifications on 0xFF01; 0xFF03 is a credit/MTU flow-control notify channel. Use the AiYin-class enable/stop commands: 10 FF FE 01 / 10 FF FE 45.

characteristics.name: Write
characteristics.notes: Write channel for info/config commands and raster print data. Third-party client 0xMH sends raster data in 200-byte chunks with 20ms delay between chunks; the vendor app instead writes 20-byte packets (default, growing with the negotiated MTU) paced by 0xFF03 credits on service 0xFF00. Same command set as 0xFF02 (YAML alias of that block).

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: Notification channel for responses. Subscribe before sending commands. Responses are ASCII strings or binary status bytes.

services.name: Fichero UART Service (Third-Party Primary)
services.notes: Functional alternate BLE UART service. Never referenced by the vendor app (no 18f0 occurrence anywhere in it); it is the service the third-party client 0xMH/fichero-printer treats as primary, and it works on real hardware. All commands are written to 0x2AF1; responses arrive as notifications on 0x2AF0. Use the AiYin-class enable/stop commands: 10 FF FE 01 / 10 FF FE 45.

characteristics.name: Unknown
characteristics.notes: Present in both sources' enumerations; function unknown.

services.name: Fichero UART Service (Alternate 2)
services.notes: Microchip Transparent UART style service. The notify characteristic is 49535343-1e4d-4bd9-ba61-23c647249616 per both 0xMH's PROTOCOL.md and atctwo's independent L13 hardware enumeration (an earlier revision of this spec listed a ...4c8a-...-3b7e characteristic that neither source has).
